content.comment_body: I'm new to AWS and [product_name], and I'm also encountering a download error. After creating the environment in AWS, I can attempt downloading from [product_name], but end up with a 502 Bad Gateway error at the [url]. When I try downloading directly from [product_name], it fails with the error: "No solution stack named '64bit Amazon Linux 2016.09 v2 running Tomcat 8.5 Java' found." I'm currently working with Python on my PC, which AWS Beanstalk supports. Is Python compatible with [product_name], or must I use Tomcat? Thank you.

I really need some help. I've tried every suggestion on the forum but still can't load my [product_name] application to AWS. Creating an environment directly from [product_name] always fails, giving the same error I mentioned earlier. My device is communicating, and I followed the forum's workaround, but I encounter the same download error. I've attached the [product_name] application zip file. After three weeks of attempts, I'm really stuck. Any assistance is appreciated. Thank you.

Hello [user_name], I haven't seen that error before—could you provide a screenshot? Which steps did you follow to create a new ecosystem in AWS? Also, I suggest reviewing: [document] - Connection to a cloud.

Thanks for replying. I followed the instructions in the [company_name] brochure called '[product_name] - Connection to a Cloud.' I'm certain my device is connected and communicating, but uploading the [product_name] project to the cloud always fails. I've tried the forum's workaround and attempted to create my PC as a device with JAVA, Python, and Node.JS, but nothing works. I'm out of ideas.

My problem seems quite unique. Could someone answer a few questions to help troubleshoot? 1. Is it necessary to register my PC as a device on AWS to upload my [product_name] project to the cloud? 2. Do I need some application environment like Java or Tomcat installed on my PC? 3. If so, which language and version are recommended for Windows 10? Thank you.

I'm facing the same issues. I've tried everything to deploy a project to AWS, but it doesn't work. All the manuals from [company_name] are outdated, and permissions for Beanstalk no longer exist. I found a custom permission to replace it, but I still get a message saying I'm unable to create a new environment. I've followed every tutorial available, but nothing resolves it.
Thanks [user_name] for sharing your experience. I've also struggled to get support on this problem. I added the manual Beanstalk permission, but it didn't help either.
Consider submitting a support request.

[user_name], I just installed [product_name] version 8.3 service pack 1 and [product_name] version 1.1.1. This resolved my issue; I can now load my [product_name] application and create environments without any errors. The environment created by [product_name] automatically uses Tomcat and Corretto. Make sure to completely uninstall any previous [product_name] versions before installing version 1.1.1. I'm still working through a connection issue between my [product_name] application and the cloud device, but that's separate from this. Hope this helps.
My last message was intended for [user_name].
Apologies for my spelling. The previous post was meant for [user_name].
Sorry for my spelling mistake. The last post was directed to [user_name].

I've finally managed to get it working after countless attempts and manually creating environments in AWS. For now, I’m sticking with the one that works until I find a reliable solution. This shouldn't be so complicated, [company_name]. Please assist us.

Honestly, if your project is long-term, it's best to avoid combining AWS and [product_name]. The setup is too unreliable and can fail unexpectedly. If [company_name] wanted, they could have provided their own cloud for these solutions long ago.
Sometimes simply updating your software to the latest version can solve these problems. Have you tried using [product_name] version 1.1.1?
Actually, I'm still on version 1.1.0. Could this be causing the problem? I can't find an update button anywhere.
[product_name] doesn't offer an update button. You need to manually download and install version 1.1.1. This is included as part of the update for [product_name] to version 8.3.1.
Has anyone been able to find the download link? The only one I located gives me a message about export restrictions preventing the download.
Yes, you're correct—the download is restricted due to export controls. Check the thread titled: Download links for current [product_name] software and firmware.
Thank you [user_name] for sharing the links.
I finally have access and downloaded the full package. After installation, it’s still version 1.1.0. Are you sure there's a newer version available?

[user_name], you must uninstall [product_name] version 1.1.0 before proceeding. I’d also suggest restarting your system ahead of installing version 1.1.1. I was still running [product_name] version 8.2, so I removed that and version 8.3, then installed version 8.3 service pack 1 before adding [product_name] version 1.1.1.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members are experiencing considerable difficulty deploying [product_name] applications to AWS. The main issues involve deployment errors related to missing solution stacks and environment creation failures. Documentation and workarounds shared on the forum are outdated, permissions required for deployment are either obsolete or insufficient, and there is a need to manually update and install newer versions of relevant software. Resolution typically requires upgrading to the latest versions, indicating compatibility issues between [company_name] software and AWS environments.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [company_name] software to easily enable AWS environment creation and project deployment, supported by up-to-date documentation and compatibility with popular programming languages and environments like Python, Java, and Tomcat.
